title: Foundations: Cowboy Ballads - The Complete Guide
summary: What Cowboy Ballads is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Cowboy Ballads songs: Cowboy ballads are the working songs of the cattle trails: yodeling choruses, waltz-time laments, and wide-open melodies about stampedes, sweethearts left behind, and the dying frontier.

History: Trail-drive cowboys (1860s–1890s) sang to calm cattle at night. John Lomax's Cowboy Songs (1910) preserved them; Gene Autry and Roy Rogers sang them to millions in 1930s–40s Western films.

How the songs work: Cowboy Ballads favors the keys of G, C, D, A. Common forms include Waltz-time narrative with yodeled refrain; Talking-blues trail report. Players should master yodel break: flip to falsetto on the chorus first, then bass–strum–strum waltz pattern. Capo 2, waltz strum: bass–strum–strum.

title: Home on the Range - Cowboy Ballads Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Home on the Range by Traditional (1873).
body:
Home on the Range — Traditional, 1873. Kansas's state song; a trail-drive favorite.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of D):
Dm | Gm | C | F

This study chart uses the 'Lament vi–ii–V–I' progression, the Cowboy Ballads workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: waltz-time narrative with yodeled refrain. Listen for harmonica fills between verses — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Cowboy Ballads pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let harmonica fills between verses. Capo 2, waltz strum: bass–strum–strum. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
